title: Secrets & Credential Inventory Runbook (operational playbook)
summary: Operational runbook for secrets lifecycle management: vault onboarding, credential inventory fields and owners, rotation schedules and automation, emergency break-glass flow, RBAC v2 mapping notes, audit log schema for evidence automation, and SIEM export guidance.
body:
Purpose:
This runbook consolidates day-to-day and emergency procedures for secrets management at Redwood Inference. It is intended for secops, infra, SRE, and any engineering team that manages credentials (db creds, API keys, TLS certs, service principals). Use this doc for onboarding secrets into Vault, scheduling rotations, responding to suspected compromise, and collecting audit evidence for compliance requests.

Scope:
- All long-lived credentials stored by teams in company-managed secret stores (HashiCorp Vault primary).
- Emergency temporary accesses (break-glass) that bypass least-privilege for incident response.
- Audit log collection and SIEM export for all vault operations, credential rotations, and break-glass approvals.
- RBAC v2 mapping notes for who may perform rotations, read vs write vs root actions.

Owners & Roles:
- Secrets Owner (per-credential): team lead or service owner responsible for rotation cadence and emergency approvals.
- Secrets Operator: infra/SRE team members who implement automation, enforce policies, and run the vault cluster.
- Compliance Reviewer: security/compliance reviewer who verifies evidence for audits.
- Emergency Approver: designated on-call (PagerDuty) for break-glass on-call approval.

Credential Inventory (required fields):
Maintain inventory.csv (canonical source stored in restricted drive path). Each row must include:
- credential_id: unique id (secrets-redwood-<team>-<service>-<short>)
- system: e.g. postgres-prod, kubernetes-api, stripe-integration
- secret_type: db_password | api_key | tls_cert | oauth_client | ssh_key
- owner: person/team (email)
- vault_path: e.g. secret/data/teams/payments/db/prod
- created_at: ISO date
- last_rotated: ISO date
- rotation_cadence: e.g. 90d | 30d | event-driven
- privilege_level: low | medium | high | root
- emergency_contact: pagerduty on-call or team alias
- storage_policy: ephemeral | long-lived | derived
- current_access_methods: list of systems or roles that read it
- notes: free text for exceptions

Rotation Policy (default guidance):
- DB credentials: rotate every 90d unless using ephemeral DB users (preferred).
- API keys (3rd party): rotate every 90d; if provider doesn't support rotation, flag as exception and require additional compensating controls (IP allowlist, limited scope).
- TLS certs: rotate 30d before expiration, automate via ACME where possible.
- Service tokens: prefer short-lived tokens (<=24h) issued by internal token service.
- Root or highly privileged keys: avoid storing in app code; enforce hardware-backed storage and quarterly rotation with multi-owner approval.

Onboarding checklist (add new secret to Vault):
1) Create canonical credential_id and update inventory.csv.
2) Create a vault path following namespacing standards (secret/data/<team>/<service>/<env>).
3) Write secret via Vault CLI or CI pipeline with write-only policies for consumers. Example: vault kv put secret/data/payments/db/prod username="reader" password="<REDACTED>"
4) Attach a policy scoped to the minimal set of principals. Use RBAC v2 mapping (see RBAC notes below).
5) Configure audit logging and SIEM export for the path.
6) Add automation for rotations where supported (lambda/k8s Cron, Vault TTL/leases).
7) Record owner and rotation cadence in inventory.csv and notify compliance reviewer.

RBAC v2: practical mapping notes
- Principle of least-privilege: create fine-grained policies, avoid team-wide root tokens.
- Policy examples:
  - secret-reader-<team>: read only to secret/data/<team>/*
  - secret-writer-automation: write to secret/data/<team>/<service>/rotation
  - secret-rotate-op: update and create but not delete, attached to automation service principal
  - emergency-root: high-sensitivity, audit-only, requires approval flow via Vault Sentinel or external approver
- Role assignment process: GitHub PR to infra repo updates policy json, automated validation, and a short review window (2 reviewers).

Break-glass emergency flow (compromise suspected or urgent incident):
1) Trigger: evidence of exfiltration or immediate service-inaccessibility forcing credential reveal.
2) PagerDuty run: on-call files an emergency access request in the incident channel and attaches incident id.
3) Approver check: Emergency Approver grants a short-lived token (<=1h) with single-use scope. Record approver id and reason in vault audit.
4) Rotate affected credentials immediately after containment: run rotation playbooks for DB/API/TLS.
5) Post-incident: rotate all secrets in affected trust boundary, update inventory.last_rotated, and produce evidence bundle for compliance (see Evidence section).
6) Root cause & preventative action: add automation or policy changes to reduce need for future break-glass.

Rotation playbook (example db credential rotation):
- Step A: Create new database user with limited privileges.
- Step B: Deploy new creds into Vault at new path or new version and test application connectivity via non-disruptive staging route.
- Step C: Update app rolling deploy to pick new credential version (use feature flags if needed).
- Step D: Monitor errors for 15 minutes; if errors > 5% rollback to previous version and trigger incident review.
- Step E: Revoke old DB user only after successful verification.

Automation & Evidence collection:
- Audit log schema (fields we capture for each vault event):
  - timestamp
  - event_id
  - principal (user/service)
  - action (read|write|delete|create|renew|revoke|wrap)
  - vault_path
  - request_id
  - approval_id (if break-glass or emergency token)
  - ip_address
  - user_agent
  - correlation_id (incident or deployment id)
  - outcome (success|failure)
  - annotations (free text for approver notes)
- Automation: secure lambda/worker pulls audit events, enriches with AD/GitHub user mapping and stores normalized records in the SIEM index secrets-audit-raw.
- Evidence bundles: for compliance requests produce zipped archive containing inventory.csv export, filtered audit logs for related vault_path(s) (JSON lines), rotation actions and approver notes, and the incident timeline doc. Keep bundle in restricted drive and paste link into ticket.

SIEM export guidance:
- Export endpoint: use secure forwarder to send vault audit logs to syslog-ng agent, then to central Splunk/Elastic with TLS and mutual auth.
- Index naming: secrets-audit-YYYY.MM -> retention 400d for compliance-sensitive entries.
- Alerts to create:
  - unexpected read spike on high-privilege path (>10 distinct principals in 5m) -> P1
  - break-glass approvals without follow-on rotation within 1h -> P2
  - failed write attempts to rotation automation path -> P3
- Dashboards: build one that correlates vault events, rotation runs, and CI pipeline deploys. Include filters for principal, path, and time-window.

Evidence automation samples:
- Query template for audit events (Splunk-like): index=secrets-audit event.action="read" vault_path="secret/data/payments/db/prod" | table _time principal request_id approval_id annotations
- Export script: small scrapers in infra repo that accept incident id and time window, pull relevant events, and assemble evidence bundle. These must sign artifacts with commit hash used to produce rotation scripts.

Exceptions & Compensating Controls:
- If third-party provider doesn't support rotation: require IP allowlist, scope-limited API key, and quarterly audit with evidence of usage patterns.
- Long lived machine credentials: move to ephemeral tokens within 6 months; until then keep in restricted vault path and increase monitoring.

Testing & drills:
- Quarterly table-top of break-glass process with one simulated emergency and one simulated false-positive read spike.
- Monthly smoke test of rotation automation for a low-risk secret. Document results in the rotation-runbook log.

Operational run notes (common gotchas):
- Don’t delete versions in KV v2 unless you have a backup; use destroy only after retention window.
- Avoid storing binary certs in clear text in docs; reference vault path instead.
- When using CI runners, prefer instance identity (instance metadata / OIDC) over long-lived runner tokens.

Attachments & Templates (in repo):
- rotation-scripts/ (examples for postgres, redis, stripe)
- vault-policy-templates/ (rbac-v2 policy json templates)
- evidence-collector/ (small tool to assemble zip bundles)

Next steps & improvements backlog:
- Move all audit enrichment into streaming pipeline for near-real-time alerting.
- Implement automated post-break-glass rotation enforcement (must rotate within 1h or revoke).
- Add per-secret SLA fields in inventory and dashboard for compliance reporting.

Contact / escalation:
- Primary: infra-secrets@redwood.com (for ops requests)
- Emergency: PagerDuty service: secrets-emergency
- Compliance reviewer: security-compliance@redwood.com

Revision note: this file is a living runbook. For any substantive change (policy cadence, automation path), open a PR in infra/docs, tag security-and-compliance, and notify approvers listed in linked_artifacts.
